claims.evidence: No legible brand/model nameplate or origin markings visible in the photo; green paint marks are unreadable.
No import sticker, VIN plate, or shipping documentation shown; also inconsistent with the 'Korean parts' claim, which the photo cannot resolve.
No video or audio of the engine running; photo is a static shot on the ground.
No odometer, ECU readout, or documentation visible.
No photo of sealed bolts, factory torque marks, or untouched gasket seams; engine could have been serviced or disassembled without visible marks in this shot.

risks.risk: Engine may not actually start or run smoothly despite 'tested and working' claim
risks.proof: Video of cold start-up showing idle stability, exhaust color, and absence of knocking sound

risks.risk: Internal wear or damage (pistons, bearings, timing components) cannot be assessed from exterior photo
risks.proof: Compression test results or borescope video of cylinders
risks.if_unproven: priced as needing full internal inspection/overhaul risk

risks.risk: Mismatched or unclear country of origin, which affects compatibility and resale value
risks.proof: Clear photo of engine ID plate, casting numbers, or import paperwork
risks.if_unproven: priced as unidentified origin, generic used engine value

risks.risk: Possible missing or non-functional accessories (turbo, ECU, sensors) despite wiring harness being attached
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set showing all sensor connectors, turbo housing, and ECU if included
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete, parts may need to be sourced separately

risks.proof: Photo/video of odometer or ECU mileage readout from the donor vehicle

proof_requests: Video of the engine starting and idling with audio to confirm 'no knock' and running condition
Clear photo of the engine ID/casting plate or VIN sticker showing brand, model, and displacement
Photo or video of odometer/ECU mileage reading from the source vehicle
Compression test video or borescope footage of cylinder interior
Full set of photos showing all sides of the engine, including turbo, ECU, and sensor connections, to confirm completeness
response.reason: The witness confirms it is a used car engine assembly, so it can be priced at worst case (unverified running condition, unknown origin, unknown completeness) pending the listed proofs; seller's origin claims are internally inconsistent but not conclusive evidence of fraud.
